title: Meaning-as-Code (MAC) — formal schema v0.1.18-develop
description: The strict, machine-checkable contract for MAC YAML files across the four layers (Concept, Rules, Edges, Physical/Tables). The CORE vocabulary is closed: unknown keys are rejected. Project-specific extensions are permitted ONLY under the 'x-' namespace (see CONFORMANCE.md). This schema is the normative companion to FRAMEWORK.md (the why) and CONCEPT_SPEC.md (the prose reference); where they disagree, FRAMEWORK.md governs intent and this schema governs syntax. Schema (schema_version) changes are recorded in CONFORMANCE.md §changelog; current generation v0.1.14-develop (adds the OPTIONAL typed-rule `subject` field — a short email-subject-style headline per rule, complementing `why`; additive over v0.1.12, so 0.1.12 files remain valid). Prior: v0.1.12 (adds the relationAliasBlock $def, the business-edge type `shared_attribute`, and the OPTIONAL edge.resolved_by / edge.aliases fields — giving a business relation a first-class NL-trigger alias slot resolved by mac.canon.relation_alias_resolve; additive over v0.1.11, so 0.1.11 files remain valid). Prior: v0.1.11 (adds the OPTIONAL concept.identity block {kind ∈ mac.identity_kind, canonical_key} — declaring a concept's canonical identity; additive over v0.1.10, so 0.1.10 files remain valid). Prior: v0.1.10 (adds the aliasBlock $def: an optional two-tier `aliases` map — scope_relative + multilingual — on the enumeration shape, resolved by mac.canon.alias_resolve; additive over v0.1.9's content-model UDF seam, so 0.1.9 files remain valid during migration). v0.1.14: the `^x-` escape hatch is CLOSED. It had stood in 58 places, written as `patternProperties: {"^x-": true}` — `true` meaning any shape, any type, no validation — so every `additionalProperties: false` in this file was immediately undone beside it. Extension keys were therefore not violations of MAC; MAC SANCTIONED them, and what they held could not be checked. Measured on the day x-grain was retired: two of four declared cell keys were false while still reading as VERIFIED, and the two that held were the two a view enforced. Where an extension seems needed, that is a MAC gap — name the wall and change the schema, which is now the only way to add a field.
$comment: A MAC file is one of four file types, distinguished by its discriminator key: concept files have 'concept:', rules files 'rules:', edges files 'edges:', table files 'table:'. A validator selects the matching $def by file location; the root oneOf also resolves it structurally.

DataPlaneApprovalFile.description: v0.1.19: THE DATA PIPELINE'S DECLARED EXIT — a named human's sign-off that this bundle's dataset configuration is approved, and the one artifact in a bundle that NO AGENT MAY WRITE: the ontology guard denies every governed write to this path unconditionally, and no unlock marker lifts it, because an unlock the agent can also satisfy is not a gate. FLAT SCALARS ONLY, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy: the PreToolUse guard must read this file, it is copied into .claude/hooks/ with no import path, and it FAILS CLOSED on a protected path — so a PyYAML import error in it would deny every edit in the repository. The guard therefore parses this file with ~20 lines of standard library, and sdk/gate + tools/check_guard_seam.py prove that parser and yaml.safe_load agree over every shape. Nesting here would break that, which is why additionalProperties is false and every value is a scalar. The write stamp reuses the question-ledger vocabulary rather than inventing one: submitted_via must be `human` (an agent may write a DESCRIPTION; only a human may write a DISPOSITION) and identity_basis distinguishes a verified sign-in from a locally declared identity, so a weaker approval reads as weaker rather than as equal. `covers` names EVERY registered issue id: the threshold is per-issue human acknowledgement and no wildcard is permitted. `digest` says WHICH data plane was approved — recomputed from the files on every run, so an approval is a statement about one state and not a permanent licence.

id.description: the reserved sign-off id. `s.` is the sign-off prefix the question ledger already uses.

status.description: applying is a human developer act; a draft is not an approval.

verdict.description: what the human said about the plane they were asked to ratify. Only `confirmed` opens the ontology pipeline.

covers.description: EVERY registered issue id, comma- or space-separated. No wildcard: the count of uncovered ids must be 0 and cannot move unless a person names the specific thing. If that is too many ids, the fix is a coarser REGISTER, never a coarser gate.

lock.description: the reviewable per-file digest sibling. EVIDENCE, never AUTHORITY: it lives outside the protected set and is agent-writable by design, because it is what the operator diffs. Forging it buys nothing — the gate computes the roll-up from the FILES and compares it to `digest` here, so the lock is never the compared value.

decision.description: the durable decision record, decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md. The gate fails when it names no file that exists.

by.description: the named person or role who approved — never "the team", never a tool.

identity_basis.description: verified = a signed-in identity. local-declared = the identity the person who started a local server declared; NOT authentication, and shown as weaker. `imported` is deliberately absent: a sign-off written by an importer ratifies nothing.

submitted_via.description: an agent may write a DESCRIPTION; only a human may write a DISPOSITION. Rejecting the honestly-stamped agent case is what makes the dishonest one a lie rather than a shortcut.

PipelineExit.description: What ENDING this pipeline means. THREE SHAPES, deliberately different, because confusing 'a tool said yes' with 'a person said yes' is the defect this whole block exists to prevent. `register` names the bundle-relative path of a data-quality register every one of whose issues must carry a terminal disposition — the DATA pipeline's exit since 2026-09-18, and the shape a new bundle declares. `approval` names the bundle-relative path of a separate human sign-off; it was the data pipeline's exit before that date and is kept because a bundle that already declares one must keep working. `gate`+`must_exit` names a machine verdict, for a pipeline whose completion a checker can decide. WHY `register` REPLACED `approval` AS THE SHAPE TO DECLARE: the separate file duplicated the register in a LESS informative form — one date and one name against N individually-argued dispositions — and the operator it was built for refused to sign it, having already ruled on every issue one at a time. WHAT THE COLLAPSE COSTS, stated rather than glossed: the sign-off path is one the ontology guard denies UNCONDITIONALLY, so an agent cannot write it; a register is agent-writable, so this exit rests on ATTRIBUTION (`ruled_by`, `reason`, git blame) and not on PREVENTION. Carried in mac_vocabulary.yaml#data_plane_gate.approval_missing and in the gate's own refusal text.

register.description: bundle-relative path to a DATA-QUALITY REGISTER whose every issue must carry a terminal `mac.dq_status` term with that term's own `requires:` met. An `open` issue, or an `accepted`/`wont_fix` naming nobody, leaves this exit UNREACHED and the ontology pipeline closed. The evidence is per-issue and individually argued, which is strictly more than one signature over a list of ids — and the file is agent-writable, so this exit rests on ATTRIBUTION rather than on a token no agent can reach. An approval file present alongside it is still honoured.

approval.description: bundle-relative path to a HUMAN SIGN-OFF. The ontology guard denies every governed write to this path unconditionally — no unlock marker lifts it — so an agent cannot satisfy this exit condition. SUPERSEDED by `register` as the shape a new bundle declares (2026-09-18) and still honoured wherever it appears: a bundle that carries a sign-off must not silently lose it.

gate.description: the command whose exit code decides this pipeline's completion — a MACHINE verdict, never a substitute for a human one.

must_exit.description: the exit code the gate must return.

connectorRef.description: v0.1.15: WHICH CONNECTOR THIS BUNDLE GROUNDS ON — `<namespace>.connector.<name>[/<config-major>]`. Validated by PATTERN, never by an enum, and that is the whole governance decision: an enum would put a vendor product list in the canon and make every new engine a schema bump, which is the one thing this grammar must never carry. The namespace half does the work for free — mac_vocabulary.yaml's header already rules that 'a token whose namespace is not registered here is not a framework reference', so an id in any other namespace (`acme.connector.something`) ALREADY means 'not framework-supported' with no new rule invented, while a `mac.`-prefixed id is a claim on the shipped index (sdk/connector/index.json) and is refused there if it is not a key. The optional `/N` pins the CONFIG-CONTRACT major, never the implementation: a bundle records which grammar judged it and pins no code version, exactly as it does not pin mac.schema.json — pinning an implementation inside a data artifact is dependency management, and pip already owns it. MEASURED across the 27 mac.project.yaml manifests reachable on this machine: 4 carry a `runtime:` block and 2 of those already carry `runtime.connector`, both spelled `mac.connector.athena`; both match this pattern, so typing the key turns no currently-green manifest red. A value that looks like a PATH (`./tools/conn.py`) fails this pattern by construction — deliberately, because it is code injection wearing a spelling mistake, not a typo, and a grammar that accepted it would let a bundle name the code that loads into the host process.

credentialRef.description: v0.1.15: HOW A CREDENTIAL IS OBTAINED — never what it is. EXACTLY two keys, `additionalProperties: false`, and there is no third key, ever, for any connector. That single constraint is the entire security posture, and it is what turns a convention enforced by a pattern-matcher into a SCHEMA FACT: in a governed connection file there is nowhere to put a secret. A future engine wanting user + password + client certificate does NOT get three keys; it gets one `ref` resolving to a compound secret in whatever manager the deployment runs, because richer auth needs a richer SECRET, not a richer file. A per-connector credentials schema was rejected outright: the moment a connector may declare its own fields, one of them will be a password field and the structural guarantee is gone. The block being ABSENT is legal and means 'no credential required' — that is the DuckDB case, and it is why `credentials` is not in ConnectionFile.required. Note the measured limit this does NOT cover: the residual secret scan over the sibling `config:` block is AWS-shaped by construction and catches nothing else, so this guarantee is real for `credentials` and only for `credentials`.

ref.description: A HANDLE, never a value — a profile name, a secret-manager path, a certificate location. MAC never resolves it and never reads what it points at; the connector does, at answer time, in the deployment's own manager.

allOf.$comment: The three modes that name something to fetch are useless without the handle, so the schema requires it rather than letting the connector discover the omission at answer time, against a live warehouse.

The three modes where the MECHANISM is the auth have nothing to point at. `ref` may be absent or explicitly null — null is permitted because the measured connection files in this estate spell an empty slot that way — but a non-empty handle beside `ambient` is a contradiction the author should see, not a value silently ignored.

credentialMode.description: v0.1.15: `mac.credential_mode` — the closed, BRAND-FREE set of ways a credential is obtained. THE DEFINITION LIVES IN mac_vocabulary.yaml#credential_mode, which carries each member's meaning and the measurement that forced the set; this enum restates the member NAMES only, which is the idiom $defs/confidence and $defs/status already use. The reasoning is deliberately NOT copied here: it has one home, and the vendor spellings this set exists to keep out of the framework do not need a second appearance inside the grammar file in order to be kept out of it. A new member is a FRAMEWORK RELEASE, not a bundle's choice; a connector that spells a mode its own way keeps that spelling as its OWN alias and reports MAC003 fact-restated.

ConnectionFile.description: v0.1.15: THE CONNECTION ENVELOPE (the file named by mac.project.yaml#runtime.connection). THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS DEFINITION IS THE LINE IT DRAWS: MAC reads the whole manifest and exactly three keys of THIS file — who the connector is (from the manifest), how the credential is obtained (`credentials`), and where the connector's own payload begins (`config`). Everything past that line is the connector's. The grammar therefore does NOT learn what a region, a workgroup or a catalog is, and could not be made to: those nouns have no home above `config`, whose contents this schema deliberately does not describe. `additionalProperties: false` is the load-bearing half — it is what leaves `aws_secret_access_key:` nowhere legal to sit, and what forces every vendor key DOWN into `config` where a named party owns its meaning. This file is DEPLOYMENT, not bundle: it is overridable (connection.local.yaml, $DEPLOYMENT_CONFIG) and therefore may never say which CODE runs — `runtime.connector` lives in the manifest precisely because an override chain must be able to change where you point, never what loads into the host process.

spec_version.description: The connector-protocol generation, and the DISCRIMINATOR that makes this definition safe to apply. A connection file WITHOUT it is the legacy flat shape (measured live in this estate: `engine, region, workgroup, output, catalog, view_database, view_schema, glue_databases, credentials, account` at the top level) and belongs to the compatibility reader, for exactly one spec version; the gate reports the legacy count as a DENOMINATOR, not a failure. Required here so that a legacy file mis-routed to this definition fails with one legible error naming the missing version rather than nine confusing unknown-key errors — and so that an EMPTY file fails at all, which is a stated reject class (MAC002) it would otherwise pass by carrying no forbidden key.

credentials.description: Deliberately NOT in `required`: a connector needing no credential omits the block entirely, which is the DuckDB case and is the honest spelling of 'no credential required'. Requiring it would force every credential-free bundle to write `{mode: none}`, i.e. to restate a fact its own absence already states.

config.description: OPAQUE TO MAC. THIS IS THE DELEGATION LINE, and the one object in this grammar that is deliberately left open. Validated not by this schema but by the JSON Schema the CONNECTOR ships, resolved from sdk/connector/index.json — which is the distinction that separates this from the `x-` extension keys the framework ruled out: an `x-` key was checked by NOBODY, whereas `config` is checked by a named party's schema, and when that party is absent MAC prints what went UNCHECKED with its denominator and withholds the claim that depended on it, rather than reporting a clean run over nothing. Describing these keys here — region, workgroup, catalog and their kin — is precisely the failure this definition exists to prevent: it would put one vendor's nouns into the canon and make every new engine a schema bump. TWO HONEST LIMITS, recorded rather than hidden: (1) the residual secret scan over this block is AWS-shaped by construction, so for the non-AWS engines this seam exists to enable it catches nothing — the structural guarantee lives in `credentials` above, and only there; (2) JSON Schema expresses most cross-field rules and not all, so a rule it cannot express is not silently skipped but belongs to the connector's own validate_config(), which runs at publish and at answer, and the mount tier says which tier it reached.

label.description: A human name for this deployment target, for disclosure lines. Carries no meaning a gate reads.

note.description: Free prose about this deployment. Deliberately unstructured: it is the pressure valve that keeps operational commentary out of the keys a gate reads.

TransformFile.description: DATA-PLANE pipeline descriptor (two-plane layout, data/transforms/). Declares how ONE produced dataset is built: what it `produces`, the `inputs` it consumes (each typed by `kind`), and the ordered cleansing `transforms`. The realizing SQL lives beside it (produces.sql_file). Read by lineage/rebuild tooling and the lineage projection; NOT by the query-generating agent (a concept grounds to the produced relation agnostically). Distinguished from a TableFile by its `produces`+`inputs` discriminators.

produces.description: the single dataset this pipeline emits — the seam the ontology binds to.

sql_file.description: the executable transform (the SELECT / CREATE VIEW) realizing this descriptor

serves_ontology.description: pointer to the consuming concept/ontology file (documentation only)

inputs.description: EVERY relation this transform reads, each typed by `kind`. A leaf dataset's inputs are raw_source / authored_seed / external; a derived dataset may also list upstream `dataset` inputs (view-on-view). Inputs mirroring the realizing SQL is what makes lineage TOTAL — required by the lineage-complete profile (CONFORMANCE.md), not by this structural schema.

kind.description: raw_source = an observed upstream table (described under data/sources/) · dataset = another produced relation in THIS project (view-on-view) · authored_seed = rows authored from the ontology, no upstream table · external = produced by a system we do not transform locally (federation).

role.description: free-text role of this input in the transform (not a controlled vocabulary)

descriptor.description: pointer to the input's schema-of-record (data/sources/<name>.yaml for raw_source; the dataset descriptor for dataset)

consumes.description: optional map: input column -> the transform id (or rule) that reads it

transforms.description: the ordered cleansing steps, each dissolving ONE impurity so it never reaches the ontology; `sql` is the fragment of produces.sql_file that realizes it.

establishes_guarantee.description: the clean fact the consuming ontology then inherits (and must not re-derive)

resolves.description: the data-quality register finding id(s) this rule dissolves — kept in sync with data/quality/{register,impurity_resolution_map} by check_dq_resolution_sync.py

open_transforms.description: impurities KNOWN but NOT yet dissolved — carried, not hidden (the re-eval punch-list for this layer).

confidence.description: Trust tier (pluggable scale; default C/I/Q). C confirmed · I inferred · Q needs-SME.

EdgeEndpoint.description: v0.1.6: an edge endpoint is a CONCEPT, never a raw view/table. It names the concept at this end; the physical relation lives in that concept's grounding plus the edge's join_rule/realized_by. Authoring an endpoint as a `view`/`key` is FORBIDDEN (additionalProperties:false rejects them): a join between stored relations that is not a join between concepts is a pipeline transform, not an ontology edge. This is what keeps edges at the semantic stage and out of the data/pipeline stage. v0.1.18: an endpoint is FULLY DEFINED or it is not an endpoint — `concept` AND `cardinality` are both required. An endpoint that names a concept and promises nothing about how many partners a row finds is half an edge: the projectors then supply the missing half themselves, silently (see `cardinality`).

source.description: the source/ontology this concept belongs to (enables cross-source federation edges).

concept.description: REQUIRED — the concept at this end of the edge.

ref.description: pointer to the concept definition (path#anchor), resolved cross-file by the referential gate.

role.description: the relationship role/name read from this end (typically on `from`): e.g. placedBy, measuredForCountry.

cardinality.description: REQUIRED on BOTH ends — how many partners a row at the other end finds here. `1` exactly one (every key resolves AND finds at most one) · `0..1` at most one (may resolve nothing, must never find two) · `1..N` every key resolves, fan-out unbounded · `0..N` promises nothing, so nothing can contradict it. CLOSED, and the set is a MEASUREMENT of what the framework can actually judge and draw, not a taste: these four are the intersection of every live consumer's map (sdk/project/er_model.py CARDINALITY, tools/mac_to_shacl.py CARD, tools/mac_to_mermaid.py CARD_L/CARD_R, tools/check_edge_joins_measured.py EXACTLY_ONE/AT_MOST_ONE) and they are also exactly the four values the estate's edges use across all of their endpoints. WHY `1..1` AND `N` ARE REFUSED THOUGH THEY READ AS LEGAL: both are synonyms of a value already here (`1..1` = `1`, `N` = `0..N`) and both are SILENTLY MIS-RENDERED rather than rejected by a projector that meets them — mac_to_shacl defaults an unmapped value to (minCount 0, maxCount 1), so a declared `1..1` ships as `at most one`, weaker than the claim; mac_to_mermaid defaults the left terminal to `||`, so a declared `N` is DRAWN as exactly one, the opposite of the claim. Admitting a token that no judge reads and two projectors quietly rewrite is the silent-default class this requirement exists to close. `N..N` is in no consumer map, no bundle and no proposal, so it is refused outright. WIDENING THIS SET IS ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO: the pending table-link proposal (C5) adds `1..1` and `N` TOGETHER WITH the judges that would then read them; adding them here first would put the token in the grammar and leave it judged by nothing. AND THE VALUE IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A CHOICE: sharpen `0..N` to `1` only with a measurement, and cite it in `verified_by`/`realized_by` rather than retyping the number.

date.description: ISO date — string or a YAML-parsed date

governance.description: Housekeeping. APPEND-ONLY — never edit change_log history.

last_reviewed.description: ISO date — string or a YAML-parsed date

additivityAxis.description: v0.1.15: ONE SCALE. This was a separate BINARY enum (additive | non-additive) and a LOSSY projection of mac.aggregation_effect: point_in_time, averageable and non_aggregable all collapsed into 'non-additive', so a concept physically could not say which. That is why one reach measure's question stayed open — the vendor says sum AND average both fail, which is `precomputed`, and the concept layer had no word for it. It now IS the aggregation_effect vocabulary (three terms), bare or mac.-qualified. `precomputed` was briefly a fourth term here and was moved to mac.MeasureType where it belongs: WHERE A VALUE COMES FROM is a property of the measure; WHETHER YOU MAY FOLD is the only question an axis answers. At axis level the two were indistinguishable — both mean 'do not fold'. The retired spellings 'non-additive' / 'non_additive' are gone, not deprecated: 'non_additive' was never a defined value anywhere — it was the bug token three separate checkers existed to catch.

canonRef.description: v0.1.9: a single canon binding. Names a canon and supplies ONLY its params; the logic is single-homed in the executable canon library (tools/canon/) and documented in reference_manual/canon/. `applied_as` documents how the canon's output is consumed (e.g. subquery_wrapper, predicate_injection).

udf.description: the canon name — canonical form `mac.canon.<name>`, resolved by check_references against the mac.canon registry in mac_vocabulary.yaml (a bare name is tolerated but the mac.canon.* form is checkable).

params.description: the per-concept parameters the canon's signature names. The logic stays in the canon; only the bindings live here.

applied_as.description: how the canon output is used (subquery_wrapper | predicate_injection | anomaly_check | …) — documentation for the consumer.

canonBinding.description: v0.1.9: the content-model UDF seam (reference_manual/the_content_model.md §4) — binds a behaviour-bearing slot to a deterministic canon (mac.canon.*), or a LIST of canons that compose. OPTIONAL everywhere it appears: present → the slot is canon-backed (deterministic, run not read); absent → the slot's prose is model-interpreted. The prose stays beside it — the human twin (AUTHORING A9). This is the determinism-coverage seam: behaviour-bearing slots WITH a realized_by ÷ all behaviour-bearing slots.

semantics.description: The SINGLE home for interpretive reasoning facts (FRAMEWORK §5).

additivity.description: Per-dimension aggregation rule — the footgun-preventer. v0.5: absorbs the former 'additivity_contract' (DECISION 0). Axis names are DOMAIN-SPECIFIC (a shop: customer/product/time) — any axis name maps to an additivity value. A stock measure is non-additive over time. v0.1.15: DERIVED, not authored. Writing it states the same fact twice — the concept would author both the premise and the conclusion, and they can drift: a target-inventory measure declared Target and wrote geography: additive, and a value anchor summed that measure across models for weeks on the strength of it. Kept in the schema so a legacy bundle still validates, and so the contradiction check has something to compare against when someone does write it.
additivity.x-derived-from: concept.semantics.measure_type x concept.semantics.axis_kinds, resolved by mac_vocabulary.yaml#MeasureType

axis_kinds.description: v0.6: map each aggregation axis (the same axis names used in `additivity`) to its mac.axis_kind term. This lets the universal (MeasureType × axis_kind) additivity law in mac_vocabulary.yaml resolve for this concept's concrete axes — additivity becomes referenced data, not restated prose. Values are `mac.axis_kind.*` references.

measure_type.description: v0.6: the measure's additivity class — a reference to a mac.MeasureType member (Flow/Stock/Target). The (type × axis_kind) additivity law lives once on mac.MeasureType; together with semantics.axis_kinds it resolves the full per-axis matrix, so additivity is referenced rather than restated.

realized_by.description: v0.1.9: the canon(s) that realize a behaviour-bearing semantics slot — e.g. additivity_guard for the additivity/measure_type matrix, or densify for null_semantics=genuine_zero.

contract.description: v0.5 NEW core construct (DECISION 0). The agent-facing binding rules for using this concept correctly — the resolution of the framework's deferred 'reasoning_guidance:' question. Absorbs the former *_contract family + no_probe_guarantee + grounding.guarantees. May be a free-text guidance STRING (shorthand) or a structured object with the sub-keys below; all optional.

no_probe_guarantee.description: What an agent needs ONLY, to use this concept without probing the data; if more is needed, the concept is incomplete (fix it, don't probe). Was 'no_probe_guarantee'.

resolution.description: How identity / name→code resolves (a join, not a probe). Was name_contract / resolution_contract / identity_contract.

default_reading.description: The default aggregation / role / perspective to assume when the question is silent. Was aggregation_contract.

answer_rules.description: Binding constraints on answering — which definition to use, what to emit, what to refuse. Was answer_contract.

axis_handling.description: How to treat time / orthogonal axes for this concept. Was time_contract / two_axes_contract (the structural part stays in semantics).

rules.description: v0.1.6: typed behavioural rules (promoted from an applied pilot, FRAMEWORK §6d). Each rule is a trigger->directive, typed by what it governs (kind), and ANCHORED to the field(s) it governs (binds). `binds` must name columns of the table the concept grounds to — enforced cross-file by the rule-binds-grounded shape (mac_shapes.yaml). This is the field-anchoring: a rule cannot claim to govern a field the concept does not ground.

scope.description: general | <SOURCE> (general = framework default; else a source fact)

when.description: trigger — the situation the rule applies to

subject.description: v0.1.13: a SHORT email-subject-style headline naming the rule's objective — a few words, read alongside the rule `id`. NOT a restatement of when/then/never (that would be prose); the terse human label shown as the rule's heading in the ontology explorer. Complements `why` (the rationale). Replaces the per-rule PURPOSE authoring comment (history stays in git).

binds.description: the grounded field(s) this rule governs — must be columns of the table the concept grounds to (the field-anchoring).

enforced_by.description: deterministic backstop (e.g. a CP-3 anchor id)

realized_by.description: v0.1.9: the canon(s) that realize this typed rule's when/then deterministically (e.g. a resolution rule → composite_key_guard; an exclusion rule → exclusion_filter; an ambiguity rule → ambiguity_gate). Filled → the rule is enforced by a run canon, not read prose.

confidence.description: Assurance factor for the rule: C=confirmed (an operator/SME/evidence-backed judgement), P=proposed (a provisional/unconfirmed reading), R=rejected (structure-in-disguise or superseded — kept only as a tombstone, slated for removal).

allOf.$comment: v0.1.17: a rule is either WRITTEN or BOUND — never neither. `when`/`then` were optional strings with no minLength, so a rule could carry an EMPTY clause and validate: a market exclusion rule shipped a bare `then` promising an evidence-boundary answer it could not produce, and the canon library's own docstring recorded it months before anything blocked. Where `realized_by` is present the clauses are RENDERED from the canon and may be omitted; where it is absent they must be there and non-empty.

grounding.description: Thin pointer to where the data lives (FRAMEWORK §5). Column metadata stays in the Physical layer — v0.5 removed concept/grounding-level 'columns' (single-homing). Profile-specific annotations go under 'x-'.

kind.description: Grounding adapter (pluggable): sql_table | api | file | graph.

sources.description: v0.5 agnostic source binding — the relation(s) this concept queries, each with its key + the columns it uses. A view and a base table are IDENTICAL here (query target only); a view's lineage lives on its Physical descriptor (`derived_from`), never here.

relation.description: the table OR view name to query (agnostic — the AI does not care which)

table.description: LEGACY, and still accepted: the single relation this concept queries. `sources[]` is the binding — use it for anything new. This key predates it, carried no description for five minor versions, and four independent readers in this estate consequently disagreed about which to read: one saw 22 of 22 concepts as ungrounded, another drew an empty graph. A reader MUST accept both, preferring `sources[]` when both are present, because the legacy sibling may be stale.

serves_from.description: v0.5 PROMOTED to core: the serving-view .sql file(s) this concept is served from (a string, or a list when several views back one concept).

grain.description: v0.5 PROMOTED to core: the committed leaf grain — one row = one ... . THE grain-commitment lesson, first-class.

grounds_column.description: (naming contract) a physical column name as a VALUE, never a key.

field_roles.description: v0.1.7: the WHITELIST of grounded columns that carry ontology meaning, each mapped to its analytical role — an APPLICATION-vocabulary reference (e.g. shop.field_role.measure), resolved by check_references and grounded by the field-roles-grounded shape. Columns not listed carry no ontology meaning. The referenced role term implies the default guardrail; behavioural specifics stay as typed contract.rules.

realized_by.description: v0.1.9: the canon(s) that realize a behaviour-bearing grounding slot — e.g. snapshot_collapse for a versioned (SCD-2) relation, or exclusion_filter for a bake-disposition value_filter.

constraintEntry.description: A data-quality invariant (validation, NOT derivation). The description field is 'assert:', never 'rule:'.

enumerationValues.description: v0.5: 'values:' is the SINGLE carrier for an enumeration's value set + closure ('value_set:' was dropped, DECISION 3). Closure lives HERE, with the values — never in semantics.

items.description: the value rows — every value has a stable `code`; label/meaning/confidence/from are optional core; per-enum attributes are allowed.

from.description: raw source attribute(s) this value was conformed from (a list when several raw spellings map to one code)

unmapped.description: the orphan-quarantine bucket — how raw values outside the closed set are surfaced (never silently dropped). Part of the value-domain conformance story.

canonicalization.description: how raw spellings/duplicates were conformed to the canonical codes.

realized_by.description: v0.1.9: the canon that realizes the closure semantics — closure_anomaly_check (a closed set → the out-of-set anomaly query; open/unknown → no check).

aliases.description: v0.1.9 (additive): the two-tier surface→canonical alias map a generic resolver (mac.canon.alias_resolve) rides to bind a natural-language filter token to a closed value code. Optional; absent ⇒ no alias resolution for this enum.

aliasBlock.description: v0.1.9 (additive): a CLOSED two-tier alias map: surface tokens → a canonical value code. Tier 1 (scope_relative, optional) — the SAME surface means a different code UNDER a different scope value (named by scope_key); Tier 2 (multilingual) — scope-free de/en/syn surfaces. A surface resolving to >1 code ⇒ ASK; a token outside the closed set ⇒ ASK (offer the set); never a silent bind/drop. Each map key MUST be a declared values.items[].code (enforced by check_shapes, not expressible in pure JSON Schema).

scope_key.description: the dimension/column whose value selects a Tier-1 scope_relative row (e.g. 'region', 'channel'); omitted for multilingual-only enums.

realized_by.description: the canon that realizes the resolution — mac.canon.alias_resolve.

stored.description: the byte-exact served value when it differs from the code (else the code is emitted verbatim).

scope_relative.description: domain-neutral Tier-1: scope value → the surfaces that, under that scope, mean this code. The GENERIC name the engine core reads.

brand_relative.description: an authoring alias of scope_relative (the key name is historical; loader-bridged to scope_relative); same shape. Use scope_relative for non-brand scopes.

aliasScopeMap.description: a scope value (e.g. a region) → the list of surfaces that, UNDER that scope, resolve to the owning code.

relationAliasBlock.description: v0.1.12 (additive): the auditable, first-class NL trigger vocabulary for a BUSINESS RELATION. Contrast aliasBlock (whose keys are value codes and whose target is a closed value code): here a surface resolves to THIS EDGE — the relation is the routing target, addressed by edge_id. The deterministic resolver (mac.canon.relation_alias_resolve) binds token→relation via these surfaces; the LLM never chooses the relation (the aliases live on the artifact, not smeared in a rule's prose). Attaches to a level:business edge (typically type:shared_attribute).

realized_by.description: the canon that realizes the resolution — mac.canon.relation_alias_resolve (a deterministic token→relation resolver).

multilingual.description: scope-free NL surfaces by language that trigger this relation — the SAME shape as aliasBlock's multilingual (de/en/syn lists of surface strings).

PropertyItem.description: v0.5 CROSS-CLASS primitive — a concept property. Identical shape wherever `properties:` appears (reference / entity / event / measure): name + type + required + doc. Empirically uniform across 72/72 property items. The Palantir 'property'.

value_domain.description: (optional) an enumeration this property's values must belong to

AttributeItem.description: v0.5 cross-class — an EAV / enum-constrained attribute (reference / entity). Distinct from PropertyItem (primitive): an attribute's values must belong to an enumeration (`value_domain`) and are typically read from an EAV column.

value_domain.description: the enumeration the attribute's values belong to

groupingMembers.description: v0.5 grouping template — how a grouping rolls up its leaf. `over` = the leaf concept. Membership is either `member_source.kind: rule` (a FK/derivation, e.g. category over product) or `kind: enumerated` with named `definitions` (e.g. region's brand definitions, each explicit or derived).

over.description: the leaf concept this groups (region over country, category over product)

rule.description: (rule) how membership is computed — a FK / transitive walk

definitions.description: (enumerated) the named member sets — each an explicit list or a derived rule

namespace.description: disambiguator (brand / 'standard' / 'political') — kills same-code collisions (one brand's 'VE' vs another brand's 'VE')

members.description: (explicit) the leaf codes in this set

derived_rule.description: (derived) how this set's members are computed

realized_by.description: v0.1.9: the canon that realizes the rollup — hierarchy_rollup for a recursive (self-referencing parent) membership, expanding a node to its subtree.

provenance.description: How this object came to be: harvested = emitted by the harvest (self-documenting); authored/tuned = MANUAL work, which MUST carry an entry in interventions/ledger.yaml (check_intervention_ledger.py).

profiled_via.description: Free-text note on how the raw source was profiled (e.g. 'catalog metadata + a live column profile'). Distinct from `provenance`, which is the harvested/authored/tuned protocol stamp. v0.1.15: this example was previously spelled with two vendor product names — a catalog service and a query engine — and it was, measured, the SINGLE instance-specific token in this entire grammar (one occurrence; no driver or cloud-prefix token appeared anywhere else in this file). It is respelled rather than deleted, because the slot still needs an example; the new spelling says the same thing in nouns that every engine has, which is the test a core-grammar example has to pass. The old nouns are not quoted here on purpose: a note that names what it forbids becomes a register of those names, and this file is published.

name.description: PascalCase ontology id — the single canonical identifier.

class.description: The closed seven-class vocabulary. `meta` is the meaning-plane class (epic #86): a concept whose SUBJECT is the model itself, grounded only on the reflected meta_* relations. The two-planes guardrail keys on the meta_ table prefix + MODEL_PROPERTY route, not the class.

grounded_by.description: (enumerations) the discriminator column the values come from.

identity.description: The concept's CANONICAL IDENTITY — how it is identified (mac.identity_kind) and, when one is exposed, the key that IS the identity. Optional (additive v0.1.11); presence enforced warn-first by the shapes. The keyless-by-design kinds (composite / resolved_axis / sme_pending) let a concept declare it has no single-column key rather than be forced a fake one.

kind.description: mac.identity_kind.<term> — how the canonical identity is established.

canonical_key.description: the column/expression that IS the identity (omit for resolved_axis / sme_pending).

properties.description: Intrinsic PRIMITIVE attributes — each a cross-class PropertyItem {name,type,required,doc}. Concept-typed relations are edges, not properties.

attributes.description: EAV / enum-constrained attributes — each an AttributeItem. Distinct from 'properties' (primitive).

members.description: grouping rollup (over + member sets — see groupingMembers) OR a legacy containment list (whole→part).

enumerations.description: list of enum sub-blocks when a concept carries several coded columns.

lifecycle.description: (event class) the state machine: phases group states, in sequence. Descriptive — recorded, not executed.

individual_kpis.description: (measure catalogue) concrete measures, each referencing a measure_type + own semantics.

derived_by_rule.description: marks a concept whose value is produced by a rule; the formula lives in rules.yaml (single-homing), this only names it.

allOf.$comment: v0.5 per-class template — enumeration: the value set lives in `values:` (one concept = one set); the `enumerations:` plural wrapper is only for non-enumeration concepts carrying several coded columns.
v0.5 per-class template — measure: must declare per-axis additivity (the footgun-preventer).

then.$comment: v0.1.15: a measure declares WHAT IT IS (`measure_type`) and WHAT ITS AXES ARE (`axis_kinds`); the per-axis `additivity` block is DERIVED from those two by the law in mac_vocabulary.yaml#MeasureType and is no longer required here. A concept that writes it as well states the same fact twice — and because it authored both the premise and the conclusion, the two could drift: a target-inventory measure declared `Target` and wrote `geography: additive`, which the law forbids, and a value anchor summed it across products on the strength of it. You cannot contradict a value you do not write. Precedent: `values` carries no `required` either — a closed set may delegate its members to a register and check_enumeration_closure honours that rather than demanding a copy.

allOf.$comment: v0.5 per-class template — event: must carry a lifecycle (the state machine).
v0.5 per-class template — grouping: must roll up a leaf via the members template (over + member_source / definitions).

items.description: v0.5: render_kind is REQUIRED. The 'formula' family was dropped → use template/logic (DROP→template).

then.$comment: an injected rule must carry its canonical SQL template
a view-backed rule must reference the pre-deposited view

planned_edges.description: v0.1.18: a PROMOTION CANDIDATE, and DELIBERATELY NOT AN EDGE. A planned edge's whole content is the ABSENCE of a declarable endpoint — 'no join exists to declare' — so the endpoint rules that govern `edges[]` (an EdgeEndpoint at each end, a cardinality on both) STOP HERE, and applying them would turn every entry in the estate red for having correctly declared nothing. What DOES carry across is the one rule that is about nameability rather than about joins: an entry must have an `edge_id`, because a candidate nothing can name is a candidate nothing can cite or promote. Before this version the array had no item schema at all, so an entry could be any value whatever.

edge_id.description: REQUIRED — the id this candidate will keep when it is promoted to an edge, so the decision that promotes it names the same thing the plan did.

business_relation_minted_as.description: the business edge id this candidate will be minted as, when the promoted physical edge and the business relation are not the same name.

blocked_by.description: WHAT IS MISSING, not that something is. A candidate blocked for no stated reason is indistinguishable from one nobody worked out.

measured_reference.description: bundle-relative path to the physical-plane reference file that measured the candidate key. This is where the evidence LIVES; the `evidence` string below quotes it and does not replace it.

reference_id.description: the id of the entry in that references file, so the quote can be checked against its source.

evidence.description: the measurement, WITH ITS DENOMINATORS, quoted from `measured_reference`.

becomes_an_edge_when.description: REQUIRED IN PRACTICE, not in the grammar: the condition whose arrival turns this candidate into an edge. Absent, a planned edge is a wish with an id.

items.description: v0.5: edge type must be LEGAL for its level. Illegal types 'denormalized' and 'literal_equal' were removed (denormalized → not an edge; literal_equal → value_mapped_key). v0.1.18: `edge_id` is REQUIRED. An edge nothing can name is an edge nothing can cite — `@join:` dereferences `edge:<edge_id>`, a rule and a decision record refer to an edge by it, and `realized_by`/`verified_by` are how it cites its evidence. It is also already load-bearing and failing in the WRONG PLACE: tools/protosql_render.py indexes edges by id and silently DROPS one that has none, so `@join:` then reports `edge-not-found` and blames the caller for a defect in the edge; the runtime synthesises a POSITIONAL id instead, which silently renames when edges are reordered. Requiring it moves that refusal to the grammar, where the author can see it.

verified_by.description: (additive) a resolvable ref (path.yaml#id) to a data expectation that proves this edge's cardinality/1:1 claim. Referentially resolved by check_references.py against the expectations file's ids; dangling → referential error. A string ref, distinct from realized_by (a canon binding) and resolved_by (a resolution-rule anchor).

resolved_by.description: v0.1.12 (additive): a ref/anchor (path.yaml#anchor) to the resolution rule that computes a business relation's instance set — e.g. the self-relation of a shared_attribute edge. A string anchor, distinct from realized_by (a canon binding). Used by a level:business type:shared_attribute edge in place of realized_by.

aliases.description: v0.1.12 (additive): the first-class NL trigger vocabulary for a business relation — surfaces resolve to THIS EDGE (by edge_id) via a deterministic token→relation resolver (mac.canon.relation_alias_resolve). Optional; absent ⇒ no relation-alias resolution for this edge.

allOf.$comment: v0.1.18: a PHYSICAL edge is REALISED or it is nothing. The two BUSINESS branches above already require a realisation — identity must carry `realized_by`, shared_attribute must carry `resolved_by` — and the physical branch constrained only the TYPE, so a physical edge could name two concepts and a cardinality while saying nothing about how the relationship is reached, and validate. Eight did, for a day, after a ruling correctly DELETED their join predicates (the join fanned out 215x) and left nothing behind. The reasoning went into a YAML comment, which no gate can read, so 'no join is needed here' and 'nobody has worked this out' became one absence — and a renderer cannot tell those apart either. A physical edge must now say which: a join predicate, a column that carries it, or a rule/transform that resolves it.

derived_from.description: (views only) LINEAGE — how this serving relation is built. Absent for base tables. For engineers/governance + rebuild; NOT read by the query-generating agent (the concept grounds to the relation agnostically).

sources.description: the raw/upstream relation(s) this view is built from

bakes_out.description: the impurities/workarounds this view dissolves (the homologation payoff)

role.description: v0.5 (DECISION 4): the canonical PHYSICAL role set is kept. An applied ontology's analytical roles (dimension/measure/attribute) are mapped down to this during projection; they do NOT enter the schema. 'unknown' is forbidden in production-status files (enforced separately). v0.1.14 (C1): 'delivery_axis' added — a column that splits ROWS without splitting FIGURES, measured by mac_admit_identity.py. This does NOT reopen DECISION 4: the barred roles are the ontology's ANALYTICAL ones (dimension/measure/attribute), whereas the enum already carries identity-participation roles (primary_key, foreign_key, composite_key_part) and 'delivery_axis' is the measured COMPLEMENT of composite_key_part. A column left 'unknown' while the admission test reports it COLLAPSIBLE is the residue awaiting a human ruling — and 'unknown' is already forbidden in production-status files, so no new gate is needed.

values.description: the column's observed value DOMAIN, for a column small enough to enumerate. Measured, then kept here rather than with the census, and the reason is lifecycle: this is the one measured fact a READER needs. An engine that does not know that one brand's home market is 'B_HOMELAND' invents 'B_HOME' by concatenation — that happened, the property PASSED, and the false absence read as 'that brand has no home market'. So the domain earns its place beside the meaning; the counts do not, and they live in data/profiles/ where a re-measurement cannot disturb anything that reads this file.

role.description: descriptive reverse-pointer role (e.g. primary_table, referenced, discriminator_column) — free text, not a load-bearing controlled vocabulary.

ProjectFile.description: v0.1.14: THE BUNDLE MANIFEST (mac.project.yaml). Shape measured across three live manifests — only `planes` is universal, so it is the only required key; `additionalProperties: false` is kept deliberately, because an unenumerated manifest key is exactly the invention this definition exists to catch, and `^x-` remains the sanctioned way to extend. Previously the only bundle file MAC did not define — it was exempted by a hardcoded basename check inside validate_schema.py, which meant the file where a bundle declares its own conformance was itself unchecked. It now carries the three declarations that had nowhere legitimate to live: `profile` (CONFORMANCE.md §2 — what each x- key means; without it every x- key is undeclared debt by construction), `conformance.out_of_scope` (the MAC001 escape hatch — a bundle may own files MAC does not define, but it must SAY SO), and `reproduction` (how the bundle is rebuilt, as CHECKABLE data rather than prose that goes stale — measured twice on <dataset>'s REPRODUCTION.md).

spec_version.description: Absent on bundles predating the container spec; required going forward.

capabilities.description: Claims validated against real contents on Open; a claim the container cannot back fails.

planes.description: plane name -> directory. `data` and `ontology` are conventional; `governance` holds the control mechanisms (PHASE, lock, sme_ledger, properties, decisions, interventions) in ONE place rather than scattered across the bundle root.

runtime.description: v0.1.15: WHAT THIS BUNDLE NEEDS IN ORDER TO BE ANSWERED FROM. Previously `{"type": "object"}` — no properties, no required, no additionalProperties — which is to say the manifest's runtime block was ungoverned, and an ungoverned object in the ONE file a bundle uses to declare its own conformance is exactly the hole this schema exists to close. The measured cost of leaving it open: `runtime: {conection: ..., credentials: {mode: plaintext, value: hunter2xyz}}` validates CLEAN against the old shape (note the typo, silently accepted) and returns zero findings from check_bundle_secrets, because mac.project.yaml sits in that gate's config allowlist and the key is spelled `value`, not `password`. Closing the object is what makes a sixth key ARGUABLE rather than silent, and it is what leaves a credential nowhere to sit in the manifest — credentials belong in the connection envelope ($defs/ConnectionFile), which is deployment and overridable, never in the bundle manifest, which is not. MEASURED BEFORE CLOSING, because `additionalProperties: false` is the one non-additive edit here: across the 27 mac.project.yaml manifests reachable on this machine, 4 carry a `runtime:` block and their key universe is EXACTLY these five — source 4, connection 4, interpreter 3, model_catalog 3, connector 2 — with zero sixth key and every value a string. No key is `required`, because one of those four manifests carries only {source, connection, connector}: a bundle that declines a mechanism it has no use for must not be nagged for it. A bundle with no `runtime:` block at all remains well-formed, readable, renderable — and not answerable.

source.description: The bundle's own source key — the token its served relations are addressable by.

connector.description: WHICH CONNECTOR, and it lives HERE rather than in the connection file for one reason that decides the whole boundary: the connection file is overridable (connection.local.yaml is gitignored, $DEPLOYMENT_CONFIG is an arbitrary path from the environment), so putting the connector identity there would let an out-of-band file substitute the CODE that loads into the host process. An override chain must be able to change where you point, never what runs. Independently: which engine a bundle grounds on is a fact ABOUT THE BUNDLE, and the manifest alone should answer 'what does this bundle need?' without opening a file the bundle may not ship.

connection.description: The PATH to the connection envelope ($defs/ConnectionFile), relative to the bundle root. The path is the bundle's; everything the file then says about WHERE to point is the deployment's. A path that escapes the bundle root, or names a file that is not there, is a defect a gate owns — not something this type can express.

interpreter.description: Path to the bundle's interpreter document.

model_catalog.description: Path to the bundle's model catalog.

serving.description: v0.1.15: THE BUNDLE'S SERVING CONTRACT — how this bundle spells the relations it serves. A CORE key, deliberately, and not an `x-` extension: the serving-name convention was the single most-replicated finding of the eight-walk ingestion experiment, and every walk that tried to declare it reached for `x-serving-naming`, which this schema rejects (additionalProperties:false, no ^x- pattern) and which tools/check_extension_keys.py PROHIBITS as MAC012. The framework was therefore teaching, in a gate's failure message, the one declaration two other mechanisms refuse — opposite policies in one framework, which is a defect to remove rather than a tension to document. Removing it means the convention must have a home the core defines, validates and a gate reads: this one. Enforced by tools/check_served_name_distinct.py.

naming.description: The serving-name convention THIS bundle keeps. Structural on purpose — a marker plus a role table, from which the gate DERIVES the acceptance test. It is deliberately NOT a free-text regex or name template: an unverifiable string is exactly the weakness that got `x-` keys ruled out, and a convention nothing can check is worse than none, because the manifest then claims a guarantee nothing enforces. Declaring this block makes the full build-shape `<role>_<marker>_<business noun>` REQUIRED and checked; declaring nothing leaves the published DEFAULT in force, which still closes the role table but does not require the marker.

marker.description: The token that makes this bundle's served relations addressable as ITS OWN — commonly the source key carried by its descriptors' `metadata.source`, lowercased. This is what resolves the already-clean-noun case: when a raw relation is already a clean business noun there is no source-system infix to strip, so the served relation takes the marker instead of a name equal to the raw one. Required: a naming block without a marker declares nothing a gate can check.

roles.description: relation KIND -> how this bundle spells that kind's role prefix, and whether the marker is required in it. CLOSED on the kind (propertyNames enum), open on the spelling, because the kinds are a fact about what a served relation can BE while the prefix is the bundle's to choose. Omit to take the table in `default` below, which tools/check_served_name_distinct.py READS from here rather than restating — the enforced default and the published default are one object, so they cannot drift. Those defaults are measured, not invented: across the estate's served descriptors the leading token is `v` or `dim` or `meta` and NEVER `fact`, and the marker rides on the bundle-specific view names while the conformed dimensions go without it. The kind `fact` exists here precisely so the table can SAY that a served fact is spelled `v`: that is the one split the closed table settles, and it was left open by an ellipsis in the gate's prose until seven operators reading that prose independently disagreed about it.

prefix.description: The leading token every served relation of this kind carries, without its underscore.

marker.description: Whether `marker` must appear as a token of a name carrying this prefix. `required` is the honest setting for bundle-specific relations; `optional` for conformed ones whose name is shared by design. Defaults to `required`.

example.description: One worked raw->served rename, quoted VERBATIM by the gate at the point of failure. The failure message is the surface that measurably transmits a convention, so a bundle that has a better example than the derived one should put it here.

conformance.description: What this bundle declares about its own conformance. `out_of_scope` is the ONLY sanctioned escape from MAC001: a bundle may own files MAC does not define, provided it says which and why. Declared out of scope is honest; silently unchecked is not.

disclosure.description: WHAT THIS BUNDLE PERMITS TO BE PUBLISHED OUT OF ITS OWN DATA. A bundle-level POLICY statement, in the same idiom as `conformance.out_of_scope`: a claim plus the reason for it, made once, in the manifest, where a reader and a gate both find it — never per page and never per concept, because a per-page switch is a per-page mistake. Distinct from `capabilities` (what the container CAN do) and from `publish` (where output GOES): this says what the bundle's own rows are allowed to become. CLOSED (`additionalProperties: false`) so a second disclosure question is a schema change with a record rather than a key somebody adds on a Tuesday.

samples.description: MAY THE ROWS THEMSELVES BE RENDERED ON A GENERATED PAGE? The sampler (tools/mac_sample.py --plane concepts) draws a seeded random sample of each concept's MEMBERS into data/samples/concepts/. Whether those rows may be RENDERED to a reader — the console's Sample view, or any other surface that shows them — is this key's decision. The rendered concept page carries no rows: the operator ruled the sample belongs on its own view and not on the page, so the semantic page stays semantic. That is safe for a bundle over synthetic data and it is a data leak for a bundle over customer data — and the two bundles produce the SAME PAGE from the same code, so the difference cannot live in the projector. It lives here. DEFAULT WITHHELD, and a bundle that says nothing withholds: the harm is asymmetric (a withheld sample costs a reader one convenience; a published one cannot be recalled), and the measured shape is concrete — one live bundle's raw preview already trips the public-repo leak gate on a real organisation name, and the same page in a customer bundle would publish forty customer rows. WITHHOLDING IS NOT SILENCE: the page still renders the section, still says a sample exists, and still states the member count. Absent altogether, this key means withheld, which is why it is optional and why no bundle turns red for lacking it.

publish.description: `true` publishes the drawn member rows onto the generated concept pages. BOOLEAN, DELIBERATELY, AND THE READER CHECKS FOR `true` AND NOT FOR TRUTHINESS: `publish: "no"` is a truthy string in Python, and a disclosure gate a typo can open is not a gate. There is no per-concept override, and that is the design: an exception list is a place for the one row nobody re-read.

reason.description: WHY THESE ROWS MAY LEAVE THE BUNDLE — required when `publish` is true (see this object's `allOf`), and rendered ON the page under the sample, so the justification travels with the thing it justifies instead of staying in a manifest nobody opens. Not required for withholding: refusing to publish needs no defence, publishing does. Say what makes the data publishable (synthetic, licensed, already public), not who approved it.

allOf.$comment: PUBLISHING IS THE CLAIM THAT NEEDS A BASIS. A bundle may withhold without a word, but the manifest line that turns forty rows of its data into a published page must say what makes that safe — the same shape conformance.out_of_scope already requires of its escape hatch, where `path` without `reason` is refused.

reproduction.description: How this bundle is rebuilt — as DATA, so a gate can check the artifacts still match the record. Prose cannot: <dataset>'s REPRODUCTION.md carried two stale claims simultaneously (a prohibition naming one of the two commands that trigger it, and a gate list naming three of eleven checkers, retired). Both read as authoritative.

allOf.$comment: v0.1.19: A HALF-MIGRATED RECORD MUST NOT READ AS COMPLETE. Declaring two pipelines and leaving a stage unassigned would let a manifest claim the split while the record could not say which pipeline half its stages ran in — the same failure shape as a narrative pointing at a missing file.

narrative.description: path to the human-readable twin, e.g. REPRODUCTION.md

pipelines.description: v0.1.19: THE TWO PIPELINES, and the only place a reader of a day-zero bundle learns there are two. A bundle may declare a DATA pipeline and an ONTOLOGY pipeline, each with its own MANUALLY STARTED entry point, and the data pipeline's `exit` is not a produces-glob but A NAMED HUMAN'S SIGN-OFF. That one line is the whole governance ruling made checkable: the ontology pipeline may not start until a person has approved the dataset configuration. WHY A CORE KEY AND NOT AN EXTENSION: `^x-` was CLOSED in v0.1.14 and check_extension_keys refuses it as MAC012, and the measured lesson is exactly this case — x-grain held the grain, was unreachable by every gate, and two of four declarations rotted into false while still reading as VERIFIED. A declaration no gate can reach is worse than none. ADDITIVE AND OPTIONAL: a manifest without this key declares one pipeline, the two-pipeline gate does not apply to it, and its ontology plane stays governed by the operator's unlock marker exactly as before — so no existing bundle turns red. EXACTLY TWO PROPERTIES, additionalProperties false: a THIRD pipeline is then a schema change, which is a decision with a record, rather than a config value somebody adds on a Tuesday. Read by tools/check_data_plane_approved.py and by the ontology guard.

entry.description: the command an operator types to START this pipeline. Manual by rule: nothing chains into it.

the command an operator types to START the ontology pipeline. Independent in TRIGGER, in INPUTS and in FAILURE from the data pipeline — it needs no warehouse and no billed call — but NOT independent in TRUTH: see reproduction.pipelines.data.exit.

pipeline.description: the pipeline whose declared exit must be reached before this one may start.

v0.1.19: WHICH of the two declared pipelines this stage belongs to. Required on EVERY stage once reproduction.pipelines is present (see the conditional below), so a half-migrated record cannot read as complete. READ by the console rather than inferred from the stage key: a page that guesses which pipeline a stage belongs to is a second home for a fact the manifest already states.

authoring.description: WHO authors this stage's outputs. `tool` = deterministic/mechanical (projection, scaffolding). `model` = an LLM authors them from live metadata + SME context — this is what 'harvest' MEANS, and it is NOT mechanical: the data-plane prompt asks a model to author descriptors, DQ findings, cleansing rules and view SQL. `hand` = a human or agent authors from business sources. `model-then-hand` = model draft, human refinement — the honest state of most harvested bundles. ADDED after `tool` was measured to be a false claim about the data plane on <dataset>: calling LLM authoring 'mechanical' is what lets 17 of 22 concepts carry an unreviewed CONFIRMED stamp without anyone noticing a claim had been made.

command.description: the command that performs it, when there is one

produces.description: bundle-relative globs this stage is expected to create

prohibited.description: Commands that must NOT be run against this bundle, each with the reason. A prohibition must name EVERY command that reaches the forbidden behaviour, not just the obvious one. USE SPARINGLY AND ONLY ON A RULING. A prohibition on the only mechanism that can produce an artifact does not protect the bundle — it guarantees that artifact is hand-written forever. A tool whose CURRENT output is inadequate is a limitation to record on the stage, not a ban.

gate.description: the command that decides whether the rebuild succeeded

acceptance.description: Where this source declares its test-verification artifacts for the generic board/gate.

lookups.description: data/lookups root — the value registers a concept may delegate to.

PropertiesFile.description: v0.1.14: WAREHOUSE INVARIANTS — the L2 (execution-validated) evidence. Each property carries SQL that RUNS against the warehouse and asserts a fact the ontology's rules DEPEND on. This is not corpus testing (no questions, no answers) and no local check replaces it: an `examples`-style test exercises a canon in memory, while these ask whether the DATA still satisfies the assumption. An additivity property on <dataset> asserts a year decomposes into exactly 12 month-end buckets with no hidden roll-up row — if that stopped being true, every canon would still pass and every yearly figure would be silently inflated.

assertion.description: WHAT IS CLAIMED, and one claim only. Was an untyped object: three unrelated questions could be collapsed into a single must_be_zero and a reader could not tell WHICH claim broke. `type` is closed; `columns` names the projected columns carrying the verdict; `expect` is used only by `equals`. A property making several claims is several properties.

type.description: the closed set of pass/fail predicates the runner implements

columns.description: projected columns carrying the verdict; every one must be returned by `sql`

expect.description: `equals` only: column -> expected value. A measured value, dated in `source`.

tolerance.description: the band. Meaningless for must_be_zero; required by min_value/max_value.

validates.description: v0.1.17: the CONCEPTS this property holds to account — the attribution link that makes L2 evidence usable. Without it a property passes and no concept learns anything: the suite proves the warehouse satisfies an assumption, but nothing records WHICH part of the model was thereby execution-validated, so FRAMEWORK.md §8's third rung cannot be measured for any object. Each entry is a concept.name. A property validating nothing is legal and means exactly that — a warehouse invariant no concept depends on, which is worth knowing. REQUIRED as of this generation: an artifact nobody tests is a claim. It was optional and stood unfilled on 0 of 59 properties.

test_kind.description: mac.test_kind.conformance | mac.test_kind.ground_truth. WHERE THE STANDARD COMES FROM, and the two have opposite obligations. conformance: every asserted value is RENDERED from a declaration at run time — a typed literal IS the defect. ground_truth: measures the world and must NOT be generated from the declaration's own claims, because its purpose is to disagree when the declaration is stale. A property that is both can be trusted for neither.

accepted.description: a dated, signed decision to live with a red. NOT a pass. Already honoured by the runner; given a shape here so it cannot be an unsigned note.

notes.description: a human note ON this property — why it is shaped as it is, what was changed and when. Distinct from `statement`, which says what the property PROVES: a reader needs the claim, a maintainer needs the history. Free prose, but the retired-vocabulary gate still reads it.

frozen.description:
repair of this property is DEFERRED, and that is different from accepting its red. `accepted` says the finding is real and tolerated. `frozen` says nobody has judged the finding yet, because the property itself is scheduled for replacement — it hand-implements a rule the ontology is about to make machine-readable, so repairing it now would re-encode that rule BY HAND and then delete it. Two kinds of red that look identical on a board and mean opposite things.

It exists because the alternative is worse: an untouched red drifts into being read as a known failure, and a repaired one costs the work twice. `until` names what unfreezes it, so a frozen property cannot quietly become permanent.

until.description: the condition that ends the freeze — normally the rule id whose conversion supersedes this property. A freeze with no exit is a deletion nobody agreed to.

verdict_from.description: the run whose verdict prompted the freeze, so a stale red is not mistaken for a fresh one

purpose.description: what this suite is FOR, in one paragraph a reader can act on. Authored, not generated.

generated_by.description: the tool that wrote this file, when nobody authored it. A generated suite that cannot name its generator is indistinguishable from a hand-written one that stopped being maintained.

InterventionLedgerFile.description: v0.1.14: the APPEND-ONLY record of manual work — which objects a human or agent authored, tuned or retired, and why. Autodiscovered output is self-documenting (the descriptor IS the record); manual work is not, and an implicit object is not a protocol. Read by MAC010 (change-unprotocolled), which means the framework already DEPENDED on this file while having no definition for it.

VanillaDeltaFile.description: v0.1.14: the CURRENT-STATE register of every difference between the generated bundle and what is on disk. SIBLING OF, NOT A COPY OF, the intervention ledger: the ledger is append-only HISTORY (which objects were touched), this is current STATE (what differs NOW) and a delta disappears when the delta does. Object-level protocol is not locus-level protocol — the ledger recorded that a transform was tuned and still could not show that a family-collapse list had been extended past gold's, which is what folded a distinct product variant into its parent.

DataQualityRegisterFile.description: v0.1.14: DQ findings on the RAW plane, each graded and owned. Authored by the data-plane harvest, which is why every finding carries `confidence` (C=measured live, cite the number; I=inferred; Q=needs-SME) and an `sme_owner` naming what that person must ratify — the doubt channel that existed here long before concept authoring had one.

ImpurityResolutionMapFile.description: v0.1.14: which TRANSFORM resolves which DQ finding, and the guarantee the ontology may then rely on. The join between the quality plane and the transformation plane — without it a finding and its fix are two facts nobody relates, and the ontology cannot tell which impurities it may stop defending against.

KnowledgeSectionsFile.description: v0.1.14: SOURCE KNOWLEDGE extracted VERBATIM from a vendor document, sliced on the document's own heading numbering and carrying the source hash. The documents stay out of reach by design; what is published is what they SAY, quoted and attributed, so a reader can challenge a claim without being handed the PDF. Verbatim is not stylistic — it makes the register mechanically verifiable, which is impossible once someone has paraphrased.

PhaseFile.description: v0.1.14: the rule-governance phase switch. BUILD = ontology CRUD permitted and a missing lock is GREEN; TUNE = default-DENY, where any un-blessed delta reds the gate and the agent PROPOSES rather than edits. Only the operator flips it. A bundle sitting in BUILD is not governed, and that is a fact worth being able to read mechanically.

ShapesFile.description: v0.1.14: DOMAIN shape invariants, held per-source and deliberately OUT of the framework's universal mac_shapes.yaml so the framework stays domain-pure. Same grammar as the universal shapes; different scope and different owner.

ProtoSqlFile.description: v0.1.14: a DETERMINISTIC SQL FRAGMENT declared as data rather than prose. Exists because a recipe re-implemented from memory is got wrong: <dataset> records the same latest-vintage collapse being wrong FOUR TIMES IN ONE DAY by careful parties, once moving a figure by 25%. NOTE — the framework ships `mac.canon.*` for exactly this, so a fragment here is usually a workaround for a canon that is missing or broken, and the better fix is upstream.

SmeLedgerFile.description: v0.1.15: THE DOUBT CHANNEL. A harvest with nowhere to put an uncertainty writes it out as a confident fact — measured on a bundle that had no ledger: 17 of 22 concepts arrived stamped confidence C with an owner who had never seen them, and one unreviewed claim produced a wrong value anchor that stood for weeks. An OPEN QUESTION is a successful outcome of authoring, and this is where it goes.

ReferenceFile.description:
v0.1.14: how one relation REFERENCES others, MEASURED through the connector and written only by machine (tools/mac_references.py). One file per relation under data/references/.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN FAMILY AND NOT AN ONTOLOGY EDGE. An ontology edge relates BUSINESS OBJECTS; a reference relates RELATIONS AND COLUMNS. They look alike and are not the same claim, and for a while one file carried both: physical entries keyed by `endpoints.from.concept` with the relations and columns flattened into a `join_rule` string. The consequences were measured — a bundle with no ontology could draw no physical diagram at all, crow's feet were authored claims rather than measurements, and a reference whose two columns are spelled differently was unreachable because a concept-keyed entry is written by somebody who already believes the two things are one thing. A reference here is therefore keyed by RELATION AND COLUMN as FIELDS on both ends. The words `concept`, `edge` and `join_rule` do not appear in this family and tools/check_physical_references.py fails a file that reintroduces them.

CARDINALITY AND PARTICIPATION ARE TWO BLOCKS because they are two claims from two different measurements. Keys alone draw every relationship mandatory; participation is the half a key cannot supply.

A human editing this file is a MAC002 error.

metadata.description: carries schema_version so the validator does not SKIP this file. A skipped file is an unvalidated one, which for a machine-written plane is the whole risk.

of.description: the CHILD relation stem every entry in this file is keyed by. A references file whose descriptor is gone measures nothing.

measurement.description: WHAT WAS IN SCOPE, so no count in this file can be read without its denominator. `relations_in_scope` and `parent_endpoints` are the population the candidate space was generated from; `key_source` names where the parent keys were READ (they are never re-derived here — two answers to 'what is the key' is the drift the plane exists to prevent). Carries NO CLOCK on purpose: the per-relation file is byte-identical across runs over unchanged data and the measurement time lives in the run record it names.

admission.description: EVERY NUMBER A VERDICT TURNS ON, repeated in every file it judges. A reader opens ONE file, and an entry whose verdict depends on a floor must not be readable without that floor. Nothing that decides a verdict may live only in a Python constant: the inclusion-only version of this measurement admitted a demographic column as a reference to a product key at 1.000000 over 104,990 rows, and the reviewer who would have caught it could not see the rule.

references.description: the measured references this relation carries. `drawn: false` means real and superseded by a stronger parent — recorded, not deleted.

references_dangling.description: columns that follow this bundle's OWN key-naming convention, are not keys, and have NO parent relation in scope. `to` is null and that is the class: the moment a dangling reference acquires a parent it is a claim, and claims are measured. Reported, never invented and never dropped.

candidates_rejected.description: WHAT WAS CONSIDERED AND REFUSED, with its numbers. An operator who cannot see this cannot tell a missing reference from an unconsidered one.

ReferenceEndpoint.description: ONE END of a physical reference: a relation and a column, as two fields. Never a concept, and never a join string to be re-parsed.

id.description: keyed by RELATION AND COLUMN on BOTH ends. Two references can join one pair of relations on different columns; an id derived from the relation pair alone collides, and a renderer that identifies a line by id then cannot tell them apart — one silently stops responding to selection.

from.description: the CHILD relation: the one carrying the referencing column.

to.description: the PARENT relation: the one whose measured key column is referenced.

parent_key_role.description: identity = the parent's WHOLE measured key, so the reference names ONE ROW. key_part = one column of a composite key, so it names a VALUE SET. Conflating them draws a crow's foot that says something the data does not.

participation.description: NOT CARDINALITY. Three relations can all be one-to-many while one parent has 10 of 74 rows never referenced, another 52,801 of 104,990 and a third 0 of 2,517. Keys alone draw all three identically mandatory.

evidence.description: the exact counts the verdict was taken on. An absent count is NOT a zero — it means the reference was not measured.

name_match.description: A LABEL FOR A READER, never an input to a verdict. Name matching alone would propose 14 of 171 measured candidates on the reference bundle and miss 8 of its 17 drawn references.

ambiguous_with.description: other parents that measure IDENTICALLY. Both are recorded and neither is chosen: value inclusion genuinely cannot separate them, and picking one would be a fabrication dressed as a measurement.

to.description: NULL, always. Not a guess and not an omission: no parent relation exists.

basis.description: on what this was detected. WEAKER evidence than a measurement against a parent, because there is no parent to measure against — a bundle with no naming convention gets no dangling detection at all, and that must read as 'not detectable here', never as 'none exist'.

ProfileFile.description:
v0.1.14 (C10): everything MEASURED about one relation, in its own file under data/profiles/, written only by machine.

WHY IT IS NOT IN THE DESCRIPTOR. The runtime inlines every data/datasets/*.yaml verbatim into its system block and keys its prompt cache on those files' size and mtime. Profiling rewrites a descriptor on EVERY run — `measured_at` always moves, by design — so each re-measurement invalidated the whole cache for a change no engine could observe. Measured before the split: 64,9 % of the descriptor bytes were profile, and of that 95,3 % was the value domain (which the reader does need, and which stays) against 4,7 % census (which it does not).

It is also the R3 rule made physical: DESIGN FACTS (column role, the domain) are ruled once and live with the meaning; EVIDENCE rots and lives here. A human editing this file is a MAC002 error.

metadata.description: carries schema_version so the validator does not SKIP this file. A skipped file is an unvalidated one, which for a machine-written plane is the whole risk.

of.description: descriptor stem this measures. A profile whose descriptor is gone is a measurement of nothing.

profile.description: WHEN this relation was profiled and WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE THEN. Split deliberately from the design facts a reader authors: design facts are discovered once and do not rot, while EVIDENCE rots continuously — so a diff that touches only this block means the SOURCE moved, and a diff that touches the column roles means the DATA OBJECT changed shape and needs a fresh ruling. v_<source>_kpi.yaml claimed 'VERIFIED 2026-08-16 … 0 multi-row' for four days while the warehouse went to millions of doubled figures: the word VERIFIED in prose is a sentence, not a test.

measured_at.description: ISO-8601 with offset, when the scan ran

rows.description: exact row count at that moment

newest_write.description: the source's own high-water mark, where it has a write timestamp — this is what lets a later reader tell a stale measurement from a current one

method.description: the tool and version that produced this

columns.description: per-column census. Counts only — the value domain lives on the descriptor's column.

determined_by.description: columns that FUNCTIONALLY DETERMINE this one. The distinction that matters and the one a discrimination test cannot see: a brand-code column is determined by `role` for the five brand perspectives — structural, a LAW — and separately by the market code, because every market code belongs to exactly one brand — a naming CONVENTION. A column redundant by convention must stay in a key; one redundant by law need not. Measured, not assumed.

identity_evidence.description: v0.1.14 (C3): the PROOF behind the column roles — machine-written, never hand-edited (a human editing it is a MAC002 error). The grain is a DESIGN FACT and lives on the columns as role/determined_by; this block is only the measurement that established it, and measurements rot. v_<source>_kpi.yaml claimed 'VERIFIED 2026-08-16 … 0 multi-row' for four days while the warehouse went to millions of doubled figures — the word VERIFIED is a sentence, not a test. A diff HERE means the SOURCE moved against a grain that still stands (a defect); a diff in the column roles means the OBJECT changed shape (a redesign, needing a fresh ruling).

source_watermark.description: the source's own high-water mark AT measurement — what the evidence is true OF. Without it a stale proof is indistinguishable from a fresh one.

measure.description: the column agreement was tested on. THE ONE BIT A HUMAN SUPPLIES; if it is wrong, every classification below it is confidently wrong with full evidence attached.

stratum.description: the slice measured, if not all of it

excluded.description: columns held OUT of the key search. Sometimes necessary: a concatenated surrogate (cycle_key = 'Brand|2025-12-11|Scenario 1') wins every greedy step by construction, and every atomic axis it encodes then reads DEAD.

key.description: the measured identity columns — the grain, DERIVED, not declared

delivery_axes.description: split rows, not figures; ruled by a human and recorded here

groups.description: groups remaining when this column is left out

split.description: of those, how many gained a second row

disagree.description: of those, how many carry DIFFERENT measure values. Splitting is not enough: a delivery axis splits too, and the halves AGREE, because they are the same figure twice.

columns.description: per candidate: what leaving it out did

ruled.description: columns a HUMAN placed in the key or the delivery axes, which the measurement could not settle. Named separately from `key` so the two halves stay distinguishable: everything else in `key` was derived, these were decided. A later re-measurement must not silently overwrite a ruling, and a reader must be able to see which columns rest on evidence and which on a judgement.
